bear_case: The bull setup entering Monday looks clean on paper: NVDA full-size authorized, SKHY entering regular trading, June CPI expected soft (-0.2% MoM), bank NIM likely expanding. The bear case is that all of this optionality is already priced. If Monday's open brings institutional positioning into SKHY at $165+ and NVDA at $210+, and Tuesday's CPI prints at 3.9% (consensus — NOT the ≤3.5% BUY trigger), Warsh sounds neutral-to-hawkish on September risk in his debut testimony, and one major bank guides softly on NIM compression — the intraday reversal on July 14 comes when the portfolio is fully committed and stops are tight. VIX at 15.84 is compressing toward a complacency floor; a consensus CPI print with zero hawkish surprises is already embedded in price action. The only thing not priced is a downside CPI surprise. Absent that surprise, the triple-event stack on July 14 is a sell-the-news setup. The second bear case is Trump's ceasefire 'OVER' declaration. WTI at $75 and Brent at $79 remain within the $97 catastrophic threshold but the trajectory is upward. If Hormuz tanker traffic deteriorates further this week, WTI breaks $80 before Friday July 17 — August CPI (released in September) becomes the next regime shock, September hike probability spikes toward 80%+, and the growth multiple compression for AI names (NVDA, SKHY, META) becomes a 4-6 week structural overhang. The DXY sitting at 101.00 (above the 100 regime flag) is a persistent dollar-strength headwind for multinationals and risk assets simultaneously. Counter-argument: if CPI beats consensus (≤3.7%), Warsh signals a data-dependent pause, and JPM delivers NIM expansion guidance — the double-catalyst (inflation + bank health) resolves HOLD → BUY at genuine high conviction. NVDA $225 is the next stop and SKHY $180+ follows MSCI inclusion inflows. The asymmetry is real; the trigger is CPI ≤3.5% YoY.
